anti_overlap: fd-agent-based-modeling-tier-locality owns whether media effects belong at the agent tier vs. country tier and any tier-duplication conservation risk — a population-tier question, not a slow-clock-host question; fd-calibration-reproof-economics owns pricing the actual certification burden (mini-filter rounds, n=256 confirmatory, full modulation battery) of whichever forcing-curve-vs-axis choice is made, not adjudicating which choice is historiographically sound. Concede tier-locality and certification-cost-arithmetic to those agents; own only whether the chosen slow-clock host (global forcing curve vs. per-country axis) survives contact with actual media-diffusion history.
decision_lens: The existing four century forcing curves (climate-ramp, resource-tightening, etc., config/types.rs:33-107) are applied globally to every country with no per-country targeting — a defensible simplification for physical/environmental forcings that genuinely are planet-wide, but media-technology adoption is not planet-wide in that sense: broadcast radio reached some countries decades before others, some societies leapt from oral/print directly to mobile-algorithmic media without an intervening mass-broadcast era (leapfrogging), and state media monopolies delayed or inverted the sequence in others. A forcing curve that applies print->broadcast->algorithmic identically to all 221 countries as a single global ramp-and-hold is cheap (reuses existing machinery, gated by SHADOWBENCH_FORCING_SET) but is a historiographically false universal; the sketch must either justify the simplification explicitly (e.g. as a stylized century-scale trend that the model doesn't attempt to stagger, consistent with how the other four curves already simplify) or cost the per-country staggering as a StructuralProfile axis instead and weigh that against the cheaper global-curve path.
focus: Whether print->broadcast->algorithmic is correctly modeled as a global slow-clock forcing curve (like the existing four century forcing curves) versus a per-country StructuralProfile axis, given that real media-technology diffusion is staggered, reversible in sequence for some countries, and historically contingent rather than a single universal ramp
name: fd-forcing-curve-historiography
persona: Apply the perspective of a media historian and technology-diffusion researcher in the comparative-media-systems tradition (Innis's time/space-bias of communication, Briggs & Burke's social history of the media, Rogers's diffusion-of-innovations curves) — someone whose job is asking whether a proposed forcing curve's shape and universality claim survives contact with the actual, uneven, path-dependent history of how print, broadcast, and algorithmic media actually arrived in different societies, rather than assuming a single monotonic century-scale ramp common to all 221 countries.
review_areas: Whether the mechanism sketch's proposed home for the print->broadcast->algorithmic transition (global forcing curve vs. per-country structural axis) explicitly weighs the historical unevenness of media-technology diffusion — leapfrogging societies, state-monopoly-delayed broadcast eras, colonial/post-colonial print infrastructure gaps — against the calibration-cost savings of reusing the existing global-forcing-curve machinery

Whether the sketch treats the forcing curve as globally uniform in TIMING (same start/ramp-length for all countries) while still allowing per-country SENSITIVITY (a StructuralProfile multiplier on how strongly the global curve's modulation lands), which would be the cheap hybrid the existing four curves' capacity-mediated design already implies is available

Whether the century-scale framing itself is defensible — print's dominance spans centuries, broadcast's dominant era is roughly 1920-1990s (70 years), algorithmic/networked media's rise is a single generation (post-2000) — and whether a single linear ramp-and-hold curve (the existing four curves' shape) can represent three eras of such different duration without either compressing or stretching one implausibly

Whether the sketch engages Innis's time-bias/space-bias distinction (print favors space-binding/administrative-empire form, broadcast/algorithmic favor time-binding/presentist form) as a reason the transition should modulate different couplings at different points in the curve, rather than applying one constant modulation strength across the whole print->broadcast->algorithmic sweep

Whether the sketch's comparison of forcing-curve vs. per-country-axis cites the actual existing forcing-curve precedent (climate-ramp, resource-tightening; m180+720 style windows) with correct parameters rather than an invented or approximate version, since a costing built on a misremembered precedent will misprice the cheap option

severity_examples.condition: No explicit simplification-vs-fidelity tradeoff argued; the sketch either doesn't notice the diffusion is uneven or notices and drops it without costing the cheap per-country-sensitivity hybrid
severity_examples.scenario: The sketch adopts a single global print->broadcast->algorithmic forcing curve applied identically to all 221 countries with no per-country sensitivity multiplier and no acknowledgment that this erases historically attested staggering (e.g. sub-Saharan mobile-first leapfrogging past a broadcast era that others experienced for 70 years), presenting a historiographically false universal as if it were merely a stylization

severity_examples.condition: Curve-shape parameters are asserted without engaging the actual differential duration of the three media eras, risking a calibration that looks smooth in isolation but fails any historical sanity check
severity_examples.scenario: The forcing curve is given one constant ramp shape across all three eras (print, broadcast, algorithmic) despite those eras having wildly different real-world durations (centuries vs. 70 years vs. ~25 years), producing an implausible compression or stretch that a referee comparing against any historical reference class would immediately flag

severity_examples.condition: Costing argument rests on an unverified claim about config/types.rs:33-107 rather than the actual global-only, capacity-mediated, additive design of the four existing curves
severity_examples.scenario: The sketch costs the forcing-curve option against the StructuralProfile option using an incorrect description of the existing four curves (e.g. claiming they already support per-country targeting, or misstating the m180+720 window), skewing the cost comparison in favor of whichever option the misremembered fact favors

success_hints: Reward explicit engagement with real-world staggered media diffusion (leapfrogging, state-monopoly delay, colonial print-infrastructure gaps) as a concrete objection to a naive global-uniform forcing curve, not just an abstract nod to 'countries differ'

Reward the hybrid proposal — global curve for timing/shape, per-country StructuralProfile multiplier for sensitivity/lag — if it correctly grounds both halves in existing machinery (SHADOWBENCH_FORCING_SET-gated curve + structural_profile.rs axis) rather than inventing new infrastructure for either

Reward a stated position on whether one constant ramp across all three eras is acceptable stylization or requires piecewise curve segments, with the real differential era-durations (centuries/70yr/25yr) as the explicit reason
Penalize any costing argument whose description of the existing four forcing curves doesn't match config/types.rs:33-107 (global-only, additive, capacity-mediated)

Penalize treating 'forcing curve vs. structural axis' as a binary the sketch can pick without weighing the historiographical unevenness that is the actual reason a StructuralProfile axis might be worth its higher calibration cost
task_context: Design a conservation-aware media-ecology mechanism for shadow-work: fuse the medium-form lens (fd-media-ecology-medium-bias) with the conserved-flow lens (fd-river-hydraulics-flow-coupling) into a 'modulate, don't inject' mechanism sketch, and cover the three unreached regions: agent-tier media effects, print→broadcast→algorithmic as a century forcing curve, and referee re-proof costing
